# Answer: generator-shortcuts

## Strongest reproduced canonical-fitting rival

The blue-only-blocker rule is a concrete plausible shortcut: emit the cyan
rectangle's full yellow cross; stop a ray only at a blue (1) object; finally
restore all opaque objects, whatever their color. Red remains transparent.
Restoring non-blue objects makes this a subtle shadow error, rather than an
obvious object-erasure error.

The independent rival matches all 12 canonical labeled pair records (six
distinct inputs). On baseline 4.0.0, ordinary seed 8, default difficulty and no
overrides, sample indices 0,1,2 are public demonstrations and all fit that rival.
Index 3 is a generalized query whose actual Racket output differs in 18 cells.
All four inputs pass the selected validator. This reproduces an emitted
teaching ambiguity, not just an input admitted by a broad validator.

At zero-based (row 0, column 14), the selected Racket answer is black (0);
the rival incorrectly paints yellow (4). The green blocker above the cyan
rectangle casts a shadow in the intended rule, while the rival looks through
it. All 18 differing coordinates and both complete outputs are retained at
repo/generators/0b8ba9bb3c63/counterexamples/blue_only_lesson_seed8.json,
cases[3]. The complete four-pair baseline lesson remains there as well.

## How the answer was checked

The standalone workspace/probe_blue_only.py implements the rival independently
of the generator, generates the four ordinary inputs, then calls public
arcpuzzles apply to execute the selected Racket authority. It compares exact
grids and records validator results. The actual callable text SHA-256 is
1fd0b769321c4e1e0e50fc1dbfb5ea510c27709fcad3ede959d318e292d1bced;
executed normalized rule hash is 757441c9ab4a.
checks/lesson-regression/before/command.json and racket.json retain the exact
command, source/rule bindings and reference outputs. The selected Python mirror
also agrees on all four cases, but is not the labeling authority.

## Whether the proposed generator emits such cases

Yes: version 4.1.0 deliberately emits non-blue-shadow counterexamples. It now
rejects every generalized construction that fails to disagree with the rival.
Its ordinary five-draw schedule is public, generalized, public, generalized,
generalized, offset by seed. Four consecutive successful indices contain at
least two witnesses; any one held-out query leaves at least one in demonstrations.
A family override, skipped index or arbitrary external subset needs a separate
actual lesson check.

On the repaired source
480c7ae04f31b1cd2d48c8b4af0dd9f71ef9365507a557c9fc6d60cb44ddc20d,
the same seed/index lesson has families generalized/generalized/public/generalized
and actual Racket rival differences [1,31,0,2]. All four query placements retain
a refuting demonstration. The version change alters sampling, so this does not
claim that the old exact input reappears at the same controls. Exact old input
and fresh repaired witnesses are retained separately.

Further bounded evidence: 300 production lessons and 1,200 query rotations on
1,200 distinct inputs pass against this one declared competitor; all five
schedule starts at seed 0 in all three bands also pass (15 lessons, 60 rotations,
16 unique inputs). These checks establish finite declared-rival coverage, not
universal rule identifiability. The three semantic declaration namespaces share
this same rival. See checks/lesson-census.summary.json,
checks/schedule-census.summary.json and checks/lesson-regression/after/lesson.json.
